inputs.name: GithubResponseValidator.userToken.value
inputs.description: An unknown GitHub user-token response payload. It matters when extracting OAuth token fields; parsing returns null unless the value is a non-array object without an error key, access_token matches the 1–4096-character token pattern, and token_type lowercases to bearer.

inputs.name: GithubResponseValidator.user.value
inputs.description: An unknown GitHub user response payload. It matters when resolving the authenticated user; the validator accepts only a non-array object with a positive safe-integer id and a login matching the 1–100-character ASCII letters, digits, underscore, or hyphen pattern with an optional [bot] suffix, otherwise it returns null.

inputs.name: GithubResponseValidator.repository.value
inputs.description: An unknown GitHub repository payload. It matters when extracting repository identity and access; it requires a positive safe-integer id, boolean private, owner.login and name within their patterns, and rejects names made only of dots. The returned admin flag is true only when permissions.admin is exactly true.

inputs.name: GithubResponseValidator.installations.value
inputs.description: An unknown GitHub App installations response. It matters when listing matching active installations; the validator requires an installations array, keeps object rows whose app_id strictly equals the supplied appId and whose suspended_at is null or absent, collects only positive safe-integer IDs, and uses positive safe-integer total_count or the input array length as total.

inputs.name: GithubResponseValidator.installations.appId
inputs.description: The GitHub App numeric ID used to select installation rows. It matters only in the strict row.app_id === appId comparison; the method does not validate that the value is positive or integral.

inputs.name: GithubResponseValidator.repositories.value
inputs.description: An unknown GitHub repositories response payload. It matters when converting a repository page; the validator requires a repositories array, drops entries that fail repository validation, and sets total from a positive safe-integer total_count or the original array length.

inputs.name: GithubResponseValidator.installationGrant.value
inputs.description: An unknown GitHub App installation-token response payload. It matters when parsing an installation grant; it requires a valid token, an object whose permission values are strings, a parseable expires_at, and a repositories array where every entry passes repository validation, otherwise it returns null.

outputs.name: GithubResponseValidator.userToken
outputs.description: The normalized access and refresh token fields returned from a valid user-token payload. Expiration values are positive safe integers or null, and refreshToken is a valid token or null; invalid required token fields make the result null.

outputs.name: GithubResponseValidator.user
outputs.description: The validated GitHub user ID and login. The ID is a positive safe integer and the login follows the validator's ASCII login pattern; the result is null when either required field is invalid.

outputs.name: GithubResponseValidator.repository
outputs.description: The validated repository ID, owner login, name, privacy flag, and derived admin flag. The ID must be a positive safe integer, owner and name must match their patterns, and admin is true only for a literal permissions.admin value of true; invalid required fields yield null.

outputs.name: GithubResponseValidator.installations
outputs.description: The IDs of matching, unsuspended installation rows and the reported total. IDs include only positive safe integers, while total uses a positive safe-integer total_count or falls back to the input installations array length; invalid top-level payloads yield null.

outputs.name: GithubResponseValidator.repositories
outputs.description: The validated repositories and reported total from a GitHub repositories response. Invalid repository entries are omitted and total uses a positive safe-integer total_count or falls back to the original array length; an invalid top-level payload yields null.

outputs.name: GithubResponseValidator.installationGrant
outputs.description: The parsed installation token, its expiration time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, string-valued permissions, and validated repositories. The token and date must be valid and every repository entry must validate, otherwise the result is null.
